PEAK is a game that for the majority of players, is a co-op experience for giggles and enjoyment. The problem I have with this game is that there seems to be a disconnect, where the players want the silliness and feeling of progression with the climb with some challenge, but the developers want to make it harder and harder. The result is that when watching people play, many of them are struggling to progress at all, some unable to clear a run after several hours, and yet they want to make it even worse for these poor players. I have disagreement in the direction that balance changes, and introduction of new biomes, appears to be taking, in that there is a priority on punishment through difficult additions to the game rather than a priority on people enjoying themselves and being able to win. There is also removal of things that were fun and generally harmless. 
 
Firstly, I want to put in perspective that I'm not a new player, and can win the majority of my runs. My concern is not for myself, but for the newer or less experienced players. I'll list some things I didn't like below. 
 
Things players did for fun are removed:  
Bag + scout cannon making you fly further was severely limited to prevent glitching. 
Cannot put dynamite in your bag. 
Cannot put scorpions in your bag. 
Cannot put mandrakes in your bag. 
 
The player is nerfed in ways that are unfun: 
Increased heat gain over hot rocks in the kiln. 
Increased heat gain from caldera hot rocks. 
Heat has a longer delay b

I really liked PEAK when it came out. It was challenging, but peaceful. I could take my time in figuring out the best way to the top. But now? There's just too much stuff. I'm getting chased by zombies and spiders and scorpions to the top. What used to be a relaxing, tranquil game now feels stressful.

It's fun when you're playing with people, but there in lies the issue. No lobby system. The only way to get a game going is by inviting friends. It's hilarious because the developers advertise that as a feature on their store page. Not having a public matchmaking or lobby system isn't a feature. It's a lack of a feature, a damn basic feature at that. Unless you've got some buddies who already play the game, your only other option is the discord. 

BUT WAIT! You can't just hop on the Discord channel and pop into the LFG chat and start looking for a group. Nope, you've got to "level up" first, basically chatting away in the discord channel until you eventually level up enough to join the LFG chat. I really can't begin to fathom what the developers were thinking with this system.

If you don't support forced arbitration in your EULA, don't bother buying this game. The devs recently added it; there's no "click to agree", you just agree simply by playing the game. They've said there's a clause to get around it, but you need to send a letter to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sweden within 30 days stating you disagree and provide details. Sadly I can't refund the game now, which means I've spent $11.79 aud on a game I can no longer play because the devs decided to add a crap EULA. If any of the devs see this, please reconsider what you've done.

The concept and gameplay is really fun, but it doesn't support saves, which is a deal breaker for me. I rarely have more than an hour to play at a time, and neither does my friend. So neither solo nor co-op is a good experience in terms of time commitment. Starting over every time I have to leave the game midway became so exhausting that I stopped playing it. Either allow saves, or add another mode which lets you choose whatever map you want, even if it's just for "practice" and doesn't have accomplishments.

I can see this being something I return to in the future, but based on the current time commitment that playing it requires, it's a hard pass for me.

Mixed Feelings – Fun concept, frustrating direction

PEAK is, at its core, a co-op game meant for laughs, teamwork, and the shared struggle of the climb. When it’s working, it’s a blast — the silly moments, the coordination, and the feeling of slowly overcoming obstacles together are genuinely enjoyable.

The problem is that the game’s balance seems to be moving in a direction that punishes rather than empowers players. Most people play PEAK for the goofy co-op experience and a sense of progression with some challenge, not to be endlessly punished by near-impossible climbs. Right now, many players struggle to complete even a single run after several hours, and yet updates seem to focus on making things even harder.

There feels like a disconnect between what the players want — fun, teamwork, and steady progress — and what the developers are delivering — harsher mechanics and more frustration. I hope future updates focus more on keeping the experience enjoyable and achievable, rather than just increasing the difficulty curve.

The combination of zombies (which can CLIMB, deal extreme spore damage, and knock you back), beetles that can also knock you back, spiders that poison and fling you around, spores everywhere that make it impossible to stay in one place, wind that blows you away and drains your stamina like crazy while climbing—and generally having no safe place to retreat from all these dangers—makes it unbearable.

I won’t play this game again until I get my jungle back (which, by the way, I used to hate, but now I’d gladly take back with open arms).

There was a lot of love poured into the design of this game, especially when it comes to the unfortunate characters having to brave deadly hazards.

It is therefore very saddening that the game's difficulty is so punishing for casual coop players with just a few hours to play a week.

I can see that the game demands "gitting gud", neither me nor my coop partners have the time to spend on that anymore in our life, making us another casualty of the "Roots" biome.

I wish the developers would have added a difficulty below "Tenderfoot", call it "Crybaby" for all I care, to have folks like us still enjoy the silly and heartfelt design and have a few good lulz without being frustrated out of our minds.

Guess we're simply not the right audience anymore.

I love the game, but somehow I also hate it sometimes. 
 
I disconnected from the game because of a network issue, and when I came back, my character was already dead and had become a ghost. I had to wait until the next map just to be able to revive and play again. 
 
I think the checkpoint and disconnect system really needs to be improved. If a player disconnects because of a network problem, they shouldn't immediately be considered dead. Losing all of their items and progress because of a temporary disconnection is extremely frustrating. 
 
There should be some kind of grace period or checkpoint system that allows players to reconnect without losing everything. Network issues can happen to anyone, and punishing players this heavily for something that's not necessarily their fault makes the game feel frustrating and can make people lose motivation to play.

Not everyone has the same amount of free time and will be able to play on "easier days" because of the map system, and turning off intended game mechanics feels like cheating.

I'm happy I got to play this game when it was PEAK, but I don't recommend it now.

I never ragequitted this game before some of these updates. This game was about chill, fun, climbing with some skill on higher ascents. Now if you want to see & do everthing and get all achievements you have to hope for the right rotation of biomes. Some biomes are way more annoying than others and there are some RNG elements that are not fun or good. 

I still like the game, until I suddenly don't. There are always some new elements that make the game worse for me. Give me a challenge, but not too many RNG elements I can't control and not too many annoying elements that just stop me from having fun. For example, the traps in the citadel are good additions. You see where they are and act accordingly. Except for some traps on the ground that can be obscured by other elements. Peak was a good game, alone and with friend. It could have been a great game, but all these updates are so hit or miss that I am too frustrated with the games direction.
